items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was part of my Impromptu Quartet, my first close friend, musical friend.

ctx.x: It looks like I’m 17. So, ’63, ’64, and it’s because of my friend Mike Garson, who plays piano. His father was a liquor salesman, and on one of the rounds, they stopped at the Half Note. He supplied liquor to the Half Note. Mike walked in, and he

saw Tristano with Warne [Marsh] and Lee [Konitz]. He – Mike was a year older than me in high school. He was part of my Impromptu Quartet, my first close friend, musical friend. Somehow he knew the – “Do you give lessons?” Anyway, he started studying with Lennie, and he said, you ought to go to Lennie. I was desperate to have anybody teach me anything about jazz, because there was nobody. There was nothing. No books. There was nothing to learn from. So I went to Lennie at 17.
